statement: With the boundary polarization fixed above, there is a formal potential f ∈ C[[h1, . . . , hN ]], where N = 3(b1(Y ) − 1), and a slice s(h) such that: (i) f = C(s) has order at least three. Its full Jacobian ideal equals the curvature ideal of s. The formal critical scheme Crit(f) = Spf(S/ Jac(f)) is the based flat-representation scheme with Gα = 1, and carries its marked based matrix Gβ. (ii) For each fixed T0 ∈ g there is an affine slice with boundary τT0ζ + v(h, τ)ξ and adjusted potential fτ = f + τb = C(s(h, τ)) + ϵ 2 tr(τT0v(h, τ)), τ2 = 0. Its internal Jacobian ideal equals its full curvature ideal. Accordingly Crith(fτ ) is the based flat-representation scheme with Gα = exp(−τT0). No derivative with respect to τ is imposed in this relative critical scheme. (iii) On the entire, possibly nonreduced, central critical scheme, b = ϵ tr(T0v(h, 0)) = −ϵ tr ( T0 log Gβ ) mod Jac(f). (4.15) The function b has order at least two. Every flat connection with the indicated normalized boundary value is carried uniquely to the corresponding slice by gauge transformations equal to the identity on T.
